title_en: Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Strict Implementation of the Recusal System by Judicial Personnel
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Several Provisions on the Strict Implementation of the Withdrawal System by Judicial Personnel

Fa Fa [2000] No. 5

To ensure judicial fairness, in accordance with the Organic Law of the People's Courts, the Criminal Procedure Law, the Civil Procedure Law, the Administrative Procedure Law, and other relevant legal provisions, the following provisions are hereby made concerning the implementation of the withdrawal system by judicial personnel and related issues:

Article 1 Judicial personnel shall withdraw voluntarily in any of the following circumstances, and the parties and their legal representatives shall also have the right to request their withdrawal:

(1) They are a party to the case or have a relationship with a party as a lineal blood relative, a collateral blood relative within three generations, or a relative by marriage;

(2) They or their close relatives have an interest in the case;

(3) They have served as a witness, expert evaluator, inspector, defender, or agent ad litem in the case;

(4) They have a spousal, parent-child, sibling, or sibling relationship with the agent ad litem or defender in the case;

(5) They have any other interest in the parties to the case that may affect the impartial handling of the case.

Article 2 In any of the following circumstances, the parties and their legal representatives shall have the right to request withdrawal, but shall provide relevant supporting materials:

(1) Without approval, they have privately met with a party or their agent ad litem or defender in the case;

(2) They have recommended or introduced agents ad litem or defenders to the parties in the case, or have introduced lawyers or other persons to handle the case;

(3) They have accepted property or other benefits from the parties in the case or their authorized persons, or have demanded that the parties or their authorized persons reimburse expenses;

(4) They have accepted invitations to dinners from the parties in the case or their authorized persons, or have participated in activities paid for by them; or

(5) They have borrowed money, means of transportation, communication tools, or other items from the parties in the case or their authorized persons, or have accepted benefits given by the parties or their authorized persons in purchasing goods, renovating housing, or other respects.

Article 3 Any judicial personnel who have participated in the trial of a case in one proceeding shall not participate in the trial of the same case in any other proceeding.

Article 4 Where judicial personnel or other court staff, within two years after leaving office, act as an agent ad litem or defender, the People's Court shall not permit it; where judicial personnel or other court staff, more than two years after leaving office, act as an agent ad litem or defender in a case being tried by the court where they formerly served, and the opposing party raises an objection on the ground that it may affect a fair trial, the People's Court shall support such objection and shall not permit the former court personnel to act as an agent ad litem or defender. However, this shall not apply where they act as an agent ad litem or defender as a close relative or guardian of a party.

Article 5 Where the spouse, child, or parent of judicial personnel or other court staff act as an agent ad litem or defender in a case being tried by the court where such personnel serve, the People's Court shall not permit it.

Article 6 If the People's Court of second instance discovers, or upon the report of a party, agent ad litem, or defender, considers that the trial by the People's Court of first instance has circumstances set forth in Articles 1 through 3 of these Provisions, and upon verification, it is found to be true, it shall rule to set aside the original judgment and remand the case to the original trial court for retrial.

Article 7 Where a party, agent ad litem, or defender believes that a judicial personnel has violated these Provisions, they may report to the disciplinary inspection or supervision department of the court or other relevant departments. The department receiving the report shall handle the matter in a timely manner and provide feedback to the reporting person.

Article 8 Where a judicial personnel, knowing that they have any of the circumstances set forth in Articles 1 through 3 of these Provisions, intentionally fails to withdraw voluntarily or intentionally fails to make a withdrawal decision in response to a qualified application for withdrawal, they shall be disciplined in accordance with the "Measures of the People's Court for Disciplinary Sanctions in Trial Work (Trial Implementation)."

Where a judicial personnel, knowing that an agent ad litem or defender has any of the circumstances set forth in Articles 4 or 5 of these Provisions, intentionally fails to make a correct decision, they shall be disciplined by reference to Article 24 of the "Measures of the People's Court for Disciplinary Sanctions in Trial Work (Trial Implementation)."

Article 9 For the purposes of these Provisions, "judicial personnel" refers to the presidents, vice-presidents, members of the judicial committee, division chiefs, deputy division chiefs, judges, and assistant judges of People's Courts at all levels.

For the purposes of these Provisions, "other court staff" refers to staff members of the court who occupy administrative staffing positions.

The withdrawal of people's assessors, clerks, interpreters, judicial expert evaluators, and inspectors shall be implemented by reference to the relevant provisions on the withdrawal of judicial personnel.

The withdrawal of enforcement personnel in the course of enforcement shall be implemented by reference to the relevant provisions on the withdrawal of judicial personnel.

January 31, 2000
